mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-01.stem: Distinguish shaft-diameter measurements as continuous variable data from counts of out-of-specification products as attribute data.
reasons: True. Measurements such as length and count data such as case numbers have different meanings and recording fields.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. This distinction is necessary because copying a hole-diameter value directly into a count field confuses quantities and counts.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-02.stem: When document revisions differ, freely adopt whichever has a newer-looking cover.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. A cover’s appearance cannot determine the applicable revision. Cross-check the document number, revision and target product, and ask the responsible person which specified revision applies.
False. A cover’s appearance cannot determine the applicable revision. Cross-check the document number, revision and target product, and ask the responsible person which specified revision applies.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-03.stem: A length of 24 and an angle of 24° are the same quantity because their numerical values are the same.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. 24 mm is a length and 24° is an angle; they are different quantities. Do not treat them as identical from the numbers alone.
False. 24 mm is a length and 24° is an angle; they are different quantities. Do not treat them as identical from the numbers alone.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-04.stem: Dimension values entered on a drawing indicate the object’s actual dimensions regardless of scale.
reasons: True. A 1:1 scale is full size, 2:1 is an enlargement to twice the actual size, and 1:2 is a reduction to half size. Written dimensions indicate the object’s actual size regardless of scale. Screen magnification or print size may also change, so do not determine machining dimensions solely by measuring the screen or paper with a ruler.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A 1:1 scale is full size, 2:1 is an enlargement to twice the actual size, and 1:2 is a reduction to half size. Written dimensions indicate the object’s actual size regardless of scale. Screen magnification or print size may also change, so do not determine machining dimensions solely by measuring the screen or paper with a ruler.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-05.stem: Grinding removes material gradually with abrasive grains in a grinding wheel and is used to finish hard materials and surfaces requiring high dimensional accuracy.
reasons: True. Grinding removes small amounts of material using abrasive grains in a wheel and is used for hard materials or surfaces requiring high dimensional accuracy. Polishing conditions a surface with abrasives and similar media. Its purposes include appearance, roughness, and friction, but a shinier surface is not necessarily better for every application. Check drawing requirements for size and surface condition separately.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Grinding removes small amounts of material using abrasive grains in a wheel and is used for hard materials or surfaces requiring high dimensional accuracy. Polishing conditions a surface with abrasives and similar media. Its purposes include appearance, roughness, and friction, but a shinier surface is not necessarily better for every application. Check drawing requirements for size and surface condition separately.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-06.stem: A straight ruler is always suitable for inspecting any precision tolerance.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Instruments have limits to their reading capability and application range. A straight ruler may provide a reading without being capable of judging the specified precision tolerance.
False. Instruments have limits to their reading capability and application range. A straight ruler may provide a reading without being capable of judging the specified precision tolerance.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-07.stem: In OSHMS, conditions and results are evaluated after implementing measures and the review is reflected in the next plan; merely entering a measure once does not complete management.
reasons: True. Manage occupational safety and health by repeating planning, implementation, evaluation and improvement, checking effectiveness and remaining hazards after implementation.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Implementation does not remove the need for evaluation or improvement; ongoing management leads to the next check.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-08.stem: If the power-supply marking on relocated equipment is unreadable and only an old note is available, hold off on connecting it.
reasons: True. If a relocated machine’s supply marking is unreadable and only an old note remains, withhold connection. Report the machine number and marking condition, and confirm the appropriate ratings and connection. Keep actual energizing and wiring within the authorized work scope.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. If a relocated machine’s supply marking is unreadable and only an old note remains, withhold connection. Report the machine number and marking condition, and confirm the appropriate ratings and connection. Keep actual energizing and wiring within the authorized work scope.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-09.stem: If the zero point is correct, correctness across the measuring instrument’s full range is guaranteed.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The zero point checks one position. Also check calibration and inspection records for the condition across the full range.
False. The zero point checks one position. Also check calibration and inspection records for the condition across the full range.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-10.stem: If a decimal point or part of a numeral on paper is obscured, do not guess and proceed; request a readable approved drawing.
reasons: True. The size of lettering on a drawing is specified by its character height. The textbook lists 3.5, 5, 7 and 10 mm for kanji, and 2.5, 3.5, 5, 7 and 10 mm for kana, letters and numbers. If a decimal point or part of a digit is illegible, do not guess and start work; request a legible approved drawing. Do not confuse enlargement or reduction during printing with a change to the stated dimension values.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The size of lettering on a drawing is specified by its character height. The textbook lists 3.5, 5, 7 and 10 mm for kanji, and 2.5, 3.5, 5, 7 and 10 mm for kana, letters and numbers. If a decimal point or part of a digit is illegible, do not guess and start work; request a legible approved drawing. Do not confuse enlargement or reduction during printing with a change to the stated dimension values.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-11.stem: If no depth indication can be found for a hole, it is invariably a through hole.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Some through-hole indications omit depth, but failing to find a depth indication alone does not establish that a hole is through. Cross-check other views and instructions.
False. Some through-hole indications omit depth, but failing to find a depth indication alone does not establish that a hole is through. Cross-check other views and instructions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-12.stem: If adding cutting fluid changes the appearance, investigating the cause of an abnormal sound becomes unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even if adding fluid changes the appearance, abnormalities in the tool, mounting, conditions or other factors may remain. Check records and equipment condition.
False. Even if adding fluid changes the appearance, abnormalities in the tool, mounting, conditions or other factors may remain. Check records and equipment condition.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-13.stem: A sectional view shows the interior by imagining the object cut and the nearer portion removed.
reasons: True. A sectional view represents the inside of an object by imagining a cut and removing the portion in front. It can make internal holes and steps easier to understand than using many hidden lines. It is a way of communicating shape, not a machining instruction to cut the actual product.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A sectional view represents the inside of an object by imagining a cut and removing the portion in front. It can make internal holes and steps easier to understand than using many hidden lines. It is a way of communicating shape, not a machining instruction to cut the actual product.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-14.stem: Applying water to a fire where live electrical parts may be present extinguishes it safely without electric-shock risk.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Water may cause electric shock at live parts. Report and evacuate from a safe position, and check extinguisher suitability and safety conditions.
False. Water may cause electric shock at live parts. Report and evacuate from a safe position, and check extinguisher suitability and safety conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-15.stem: The material’s mechanical and metal processing category lists many examples of work, including casting, forging, cutting, sheet-metal work, maintenance, inspection, assembly, molding, painting, packaging, heat treatment, rolling and extrusion.
reasons: True. The source lists many examples in the machining and metalworking category: casting, forging, cutting, sheet metal, maintenance, inspection, assembly, molding, painting, packaging, heat treatment, rolling and extrusion. Experience in one process does not authorize every type of work. Check the assigned job and required training.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The source lists many examples in the machining and metalworking category: casting, forging, cutting, sheet metal, maintenance, inspection, assembly, molding, painting, packaging, heat treatment, rolling and extrusion. Experience in one process does not authorize every type of work. Check the assigned job and required training.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-16.stem: Control conditions for another product can be applied unconditionally if the process names are similar.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even with the same process name, specifications and control conditions may differ by product. Check applicability to the product, process and document revision.
False. Even with the same process name, specifications and control conditions may differ by product. Check applicability to the product, process and document revision.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-17.stem: In OJT, the instructor explains and demonstrates, the learner performs within the prescribed scope, and the instructor checks.
reasons:
True. When learning new work, understand why the steps follow that order rather than only memorizing the sequence. Before practice, confirm the pre-work inspection, prohibited actions, and response to abnormalities.
In OJT, the instructor explains and demonstrates, the learner practices within the specified scope, and the instructor checks the result. Having seen a task is not the same as being able to perform it safely alone. If an operation is unclear, stop and ask before attempting it.
After listening, explaining the procedure back in your own words helps reveal misunderstandings. In particular, do not rely on a vague acknowledgment when confirming values, units, part orientation, and stopping conditions.
Reading this material does not replace the training or qualifications required at the workplace. Confirm the work you may perform and the required training with the responsible person according to the equipment and working conditions.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. When learning new work, understand why the steps follow that order rather than only memorizing the sequence. Before practice, confirm the pre-work inspection, prohibited actions, and response to abnormalities.
In OJT, the instructor explains and demonstrates, the learner practices within the specified scope, and the instructor checks the result. Having seen a task is not the same as being able to perform it safely alone. If an operation is unclear, stop and ask before attempting it.
After listening, explaining the procedure back in your own words helps reveal misunderstandings. In particular, do not rely on a vague acknowledgment when confirming values, units, part orientation, and stopping conditions.
Reading this material does not replace the training or qualifications required at the workplace. Confirm the work you may perform and the required training with the responsible person according to the equipment and working conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-18.stem: Even when diameter and length are within specified ranges, requirements for surface flatness, axis orientation, position and other characteristics are not necessarily met.
reasons: True. Even if a diameter or length is within its specified range, requirements for surface flatness, axis orientation or position may not be met. Geometrical tolerances indicate characteristics such as straightness, flatness, roundness, parallelism, perpendicularity and position. Different types evaluate different properties, so one dimensional measurement does not mean everything has been checked.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Even if a diameter or length is within its specified range, requirements for surface flatness, axis orientation or position may not be met. Geometrical tolerances indicate characteristics such as straightness, flatness, roundness, parallelism, perpendicularity and position. Different types evaluate different properties, so one dimensional measurement does not mean everything has been checked.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-19.stem: Direct current flows in a constant direction, so it presents no hazard to the human body.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Direct current also presents electric-shock and other hazards. Constant flow direction does not guarantee safety for the human body.
False. Direct current also presents electric-shock and other hazards. Constant flow direction does not guarantee safety for the human body.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-20.stem: Aqueous solutions invariably have a pH between 0 and 14 regardless of conditions.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The introductory example’s conditions of room temperature and dilute aqueous solutions cannot be generalized to every liquid. Retain the temperature, solution conditions and measurement method.

False. The introductory example’s conditions of room temperature and dilute aqueous solutions cannot be generalized to every liquid. Retain the temperature, solution conditions and measurement method.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-21.stem: Design quality concerns intended performance and specifications; manufacturing quality concerns their realization in actual products; logistics quality concerns delivery of the correct items in the correct quantity, on time and in the correct condition.
reasons: True. Quality is not determined solely by the convenience of the manufacturer. The starting point is meeting users’ requirements. Design quality concerns the intended performance and specification; manufacturing quality concerns how these are achieved in actual products; logistics quality concerns delivering the correct items in the correct quantity, on time, and in the required condition. Meeting dimensional requirements alone does not meet the entire requirement if the necessary quantity is not delivered.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Quality is not determined solely by the convenience of the manufacturer. The starting point is meeting users’ requirements. Design quality concerns the intended performance and specification; manufacturing quality concerns how these are achieved in actual products; logistics quality concerns delivering the correct items in the correct quantity, on time, and in the required condition. Meeting dimensional requirements alone does not meet the entire requirement if the necessary quantity is not delivered.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-22.stem: For copied or reduced-size drawings, check that lines and lettering remain sufficiently readable.
reasons: True. For the mechanical drawings covered in this textbook, A-series paper is preferred, in a size that clearly shows the object. Normally the long edge is horizontal; A4 may also be used in portrait orientation. A larger sheet does not make the information more accurate. On copied or reduced drawings, check that the lines and lettering remain clearly readable.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. For the mechanical drawings covered in this textbook, A-series paper is preferred, in a size that clearly shows the object. Normally the long edge is horizontal; A4 may also be used in portrait orientation. A larger sheet does not make the information more accurate. On copied or reduced drawings, check that the lines and lettering remain clearly readable.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-23.stem: A resistor can be replaced without checking required ratings if its resistance value is the same.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even with the same resistance, required ratings such as power and operating conditions may differ. Do not replace a resistor without checking the specified requirements.
False. Even with the same resistance, required ratings such as power and operating conditions may differ. Do not replace a resistor without checking the specified requirements.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-24.stem: A single description such as “light” or “hard” is insufficient to judge suitability for an application.
reasons: True. Density is mass per unit volume. Objects of the same volume can have different masses when their materials differ. Elasticity means deformation recovers after force is removed; plasticity means deformation remains. Hardness and toughness—the ability to resist fracture under impact and similar loading—are also different properties. “Light” or “hard” alone does not establish suitability for an application.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Density is mass per unit volume. Objects of the same volume can have different masses when their materials differ. Elasticity means deformation recovers after force is removed; plasticity means deformation remains. Hardness and toughness—the ability to resist fracture under impact and similar loading—are also different properties. “Light” or “hard” alone does not establish suitability for an application.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-25.stem: All extinguishers can be used in the same way regardless of the type of fire.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Extinguishers have suitability requirements for different fires. Inappropriate methods, such as water on oil or live electrical parts, are dangerous.
False. Extinguishers have suitability requirements for different fires. Inappropriate methods, such as water on oil or live electrical parts, are dangerous.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-26.stem: Surface roughness describes fine surface irregularities and relates to friction, wear, lubrication, appearance and other characteristics.
reasons: True. Surface roughness describes small surface irregularities and relates to friction, wear, lubrication, and appearance. Ra is arithmetic mean roughness and Rz is maximum-height roughness. Check the parameter, unit, and measurement conditions against the drawing requirement. A smaller roughness value is not unconditionally better for every function.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Surface roughness describes small surface irregularities and relates to friction, wear, lubrication, and appearance. Ra is arithmetic mean roughness and Rz is maximum-height roughness. Check the parameter, unit, and measurement conditions against the drawing requirement. A smaller roughness value is not unconditionally better for every function.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-27.stem: If a scatter diagram shows a relationship, causation between the two quantities has been proven.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. A scatter diagram gives a clue to a relationship between two quantities. A cause cannot be established without investigating other conditions and facts.
False. A scatter diagram gives a clue to a relationship between two quantities. A cause cannot be established without investigating other conditions and facts.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-28.stem: Having ISO 9001 information allows dimensional inspection of individual components to be omitted.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. ISO 9001 concerns quality management systems. Whether the actual product meets specified dimensions must be checked through the necessary inspection.
False. ISO 9001 concerns quality management systems. Whether the actual product meets specified dimensions must be checked through the necessary inspection.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-29.stem: Merely having a work procedure document is insufficient unless it can be read at the workplace when needed.
reasons: True. A procedure states who does what, when and how. Merely possessing a document is insufficient if it cannot be read when needed at the work location. Check the equipment, product and version covered, and report failed displays or unreadable paper. Do not fill in unconfirmed conditions from memory alone.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A procedure states who does what, when and how. Merely possessing a document is insufficient if it cannot be read when needed at the work location. Check the equipment, product and version covered, and report failed displays or unreadable paper. Do not fill in unconfirmed conditions from memory alone.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-30.stem: For a flatness specification, the operator must always add an independently chosen datum.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Flatness concerns a feature’s own form and does not call for an operator to add an unnecessary datum. Follow the drawing’s formal instructions.
False. Flatness concerns a feature’s own form and does not call for an operator to add an unnecessary datum. Follow the drawing’s formal instructions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-01.stem: Usable and chipped tools are mixed together in a toolbox. Which improvement also prevents reuse of damaged tools?
options: Put everything together in one box.
Return damaged tools if they look similar.
Identify and segregate damaged tools, and define fixed locations and checking methods for needed tools.
Discard even needed tools without authorization.
reasons: Simply putting them together does not remove the situation in which a damaged tool can be selected again.
Do not return a chipped tool as usable even if it looks similar.
Combining identification and segregation of damaged tools with storage locations and condition checks for needed tools helps prevent reuse.
Sorting means distinguishing needed from unneeded items, not discarding needed tools without authorization.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-02.stem: Defects were recorded as 12 faint-print cases, 6 dirt cases and 2 irregular-shape cases. What is the cumulative percentage through dirt?
reasons: Of all 20 cases, faint print 12 + dirt 6 = 18 cases, giving a cumulative percentage of 90%.
60% represents only the 12 faint-print cases, not the cumulative total through dirt.
30% represents only the 6 dirt cases and does not include faint print.
20% is not the result of dividing the cumulative 18 cases by all 20 cases.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-03.stem: A failed light prevents viewing one item on an inspection checklist. Which recording and start decision is appropriate?
options: Mark it normal because it was normal yesterday.
Record why it is unverified and consult about the checking method and whether operation is permitted.
Record it as seen and view it later.
reasons: Yesterday’s normal condition does not prove today’s condition at the location that could not be checked.
Deleting a specified item does not resolve the unverified condition; an operating decision is also needed.
Retain the reason it is unverified and consult the responsible person about the checking method and whether operation is permitted.
Recording something as checked when it was not viewed does not match what was actually done.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-04.stem: Finished components touch and become scratched when placed together in a box. Which packaging consideration is appropriate?
options: Improve only the appearance of the outer box.
Check individual protection such as dividers, movement, identification and quantity.
reasons: Improving only the outer box’s appearance does not prevent components touching inside.
Do not combine counts for similar part numbers with different specifications; maintain identification and quantities.
Removing labels loses identification information and increases mix-up risk.
Consider individual protection and methods to restrain movement inside the box, and also check identification and quantity.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-05.stem: What information should be checked when judging a threaded NO-GO gauge?
options: Only the explanation for plain holes.
Only the final position after forceful tightening.
The specified insertion behavior, number of turns and other conditions for that gauge.
Only whether the GO gauge entered.
reasons: Threads have their own insertion, turn-count and other conditions; a plain-hole explanation alone is insufficient.
Forceful tightening risks damage and misjudgment; do not change acceptance conditions by force.
Check the GO and NO-GO sides under the conditions specified for that thread and gauge.
The GO-side result alone does not replace the required NO-GO-side check.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-06.stem: There is foreign matter on a depth gauge’s reference surface. Which measurement plan is appropriate?
options: Subtract a convenient number from the reading.
Guarantee the depth with the foreign matter still present.
Prepare the reference surface and instrument by the specified method and check contact and the starting reference.
reasons: Subtracting an unsupported allowance for foreign matter does not constitute correct measurement.
Foreign matter changes contact with the reference surface and causes an erroneous depth reading.
Height and depth have different references and targets; do not copy one to the other.
Prepare the reference surface and instrument condition, then measure depth with correct contact and reference.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-07.stem: Someone is about to enter the previous reading even though inspection was not performed. What should be done?
options: Enter it if the trend is similar.
Change the criteria to meet the target.
Erase the unverified field and ship.
Match records to actual work, retain the unverified status and report.
reasons: Expecting the same trend as before is not an actual measurement result for this inspection.
A target does not justify changing approved criteria.
Erasing an unverified field does not complete inspection and can release unjudged items.
Retain and report the fact that inspection was not performed, and record only results actually obtained.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-08.stem: Which record correctly converts a measurement time of 1250 ms to seconds?
reasons: Changing only the unit to seconds without changing the number makes it 1000 times larger.
0.125 s is one tenth of the correct 1.25 s.
12.5 s is ten times the correct 1.25 s.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-09.stem: The reference is 32.00 mm and the difference is −0.03 mm. Which calculation and record are appropriate?
options: 32.03 mm, recorded as a positive difference.
31.97 mm, with the negative difference recorded.
Record 0.03 mm as the full dimension.
reasons: This adds a negative difference as positive, reversing the specified sign.
32.00 + (−0.03) = 31.97 mm. Record the corresponding reference and negative difference as well.
0.03 mm is the magnitude of the difference, not the full dimension.
Since the difference is not zero, the dimension cannot remain at the reference value of 32.00 mm.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-10.stem: You want to apply a new functional coating at a thickness different from its specified conditions. Which check is appropriate?
options: If it is named functional, it performs under all conditions.
Cross-check the coating, substrate, film thickness, drying and curing against requirements.
Mix freely if the color is the same.
Omit grounding or ventilation without authorization.
reasons: The name functional alone does not establish performance at unspecified film thicknesses or conditions.
Check how the coating, substrate, film thickness, drying and curing conditions correspond to requirements.
The same color does not mean the same composition; unauthorized mixing compromises conformity and safety.
Grounding and ventilation are safety conditions for the painting method; do not omit them without authorization.
